narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: standing at the buttressed base of a Hometree and looking straight up the trunk through tier after tier of life into a vaulted ceiling of foliage — the reader's first felt sense that the forest is built like a cathedral, with floors.
subject: An extreme upward view straight up the trunk of a colossal Pandoran Hometree from its base: dozens of woody columns braid together and rise out of sight; the trunk passes through stacked tiers of hanging foliage and branch galleries; at the very top, daylight breaks through a vaulted ceiling of leaves in long pale shafts, where tiny winged shapes wheel in the bright crown; the foreground forest floor is dim, damp, and faintly glowing.
scene: Looking up the central axis of a giant tree, the trunk converging toward a distant bright crown, layers of foliage receding upward.
camera: A dramatic worm's-eye upward view from the forest floor, strong vertical perspective convergence.
light: Bright shafts of daylight breaking through the high canopy at the top, dimming steeply downward to a cool, faintly bioluminescent floor.
palette: Cool Pandora cyan and living teal in the lit upper tiers, void-indigo shadow and faint glow at the dim floor.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, atmospheric and reverent.
detail_level: Crisp on the braided trunk and nearer foliage tiers; dissolving into light and haze at the crown.
composition: Trunk dead-centre running bottom to top, radial convergence toward the bright crown, dim foreground floor with open dark space for a caption.
consistency_notes: Architecture/landscape plate, figures minimal. The cathedral-interior mood; same Hometree look as the cover.
